comment: Rules of the new game (ADR 0028, docs/projekt-gry.md). Time: 10 ticks a second; rates are per minute of play. Amounts are whole units (two decimals allowed). density: how many times more hexes than the legacy map of the same size (a hex is room for one building). economyEveryTicks, populationEveryTicks: rhythms of docs/wydajnosc.md. Start: the stock and people of a new tribe. Food: every person eats foodPerPersonPerMinute, paid once a minute at the ration (see rations); people told to gather pick up food, wood and stone around their settlement (forage). Growth: a fed settlement below its housing grows growthPercentPerMinute of its people a minute (at least minGrowthPerMinute); it does not grow while it has no food (deaths from hunger come at the rations; starvePercentPerMinute is not used). resumeCostPercent: resuming a paused construction costs this much of the building's price again. Settlement levels: radius in hexes of the territory, housing and storage given by the settlement itself, the price of the upgrade. Buildings: workers (jobs), price, buildSeconds, terrain rules (biomes, relief, needsWater = next to a lake, sea or river, deposit = a surface deposit on the hex, minFertility), production per worker per minute, deposit bonus in percent, housing and storage they add. bonusRelief and bonusReliefPercent: extra production on hills or mountains. Storage: goods lie in the settlement where they were made; every finished building adds buildingStorage of room for each good unless it gives its own storage (storehouses). Construction materials are carried by porters from the nearest storehouse (or the settlement centre); the work goes as far as the delivered materials allow. groups: tags that technology effects can aim at (e.g. melee, tools).

foundSettlement.comment: Settlers found a camp at least minDistance hexes from every other settlement centre, on land nobody owns; their people live there.

terrainCost.comment: Walking cost of a hex in percent of a flat open hex.

research.comment: A technology needs experience in the technologies before it (worker-minutes in their buildings), then its price in goods and its time. It is cheaper by neighbourDiscountPercent for every known people that knows it (at most maxNeighbourDiscountPercent). One research at a time. maxSupportPercent: schools and academies speed a branch of research at most this much.

thinkers.comment: A people has one thinker. Rarity sets how much cheaper (costPercent) and how much less experience (experiencePercent) research needs; some take less experience but cost more. A thinker retires after retireMinutes; the successor (II, III…) keeps the school but each generation loses generationLossPercent of the edge. A new candidate shows up every offerMinutes; hiring costs hirePrice times the rarity's priceTimes.

advisors.comment: A people has at most one advisor. A candidate shows up every offerMinutes with one or two fields (economy, growth, research, expansion); hiring costs hirePrice times the rarity's priceTimes, and the advisor eats upkeepFoodPerMinute. The advisor gives one piece of advice at a time, only in its fields.

war.comment: Units fight once a second (combatEveryTicks). A side deals people × strength × (100 + terrain bonus + upgrades) / 100 × luck (lowLuckPercent..highLuckPercent) hundredths of a person, killed on the other side. Melee reaches the next hex, ranged units their range. A settlement under attack defends with defenderPercent of its people at defenderStrength each, raised by its finished fortifications; at captureBelowPeople it is taken. Soldiers are fed by rations (see rations). Attacking a people without a declared war is a surprise attack: the victim and everyone who met both remember it (reputation).

events.comment: Every people draws one event from the shared pool every everyMinutes (a random minute within the spread), never one another people has right now. An event lasts its seconds. productionPercent changes the production of the listed goods, eatPercent what people eat, losePercentPerMinute kills that share of people a minute, destroyBuilding burns one random finished building at the start. field: the advisor field that gives advice on it.

pool.name: Drought
pool.advice: Drought: build fishing huts or stop growing for a while; the stores must last.

pool.name: Hard winter
pool.advice: A hard winter: people eat more. Keep food stores high and do not train settlers now.

pool.name: Epidemic
pool.advice: Sickness spreads: the fewer people we move around, the better; wait it out.

pool.name: Fire
pool.advice: A fire took a building: rebuild what we need most first.

pool.name: Flood
pool.advice: The rivers flood: fields and clay pits work at half. Use the stores.

diplomacy.comment: Peoples consider a treaty only when they have known each other for knownMinutes, their settlements are at most borderHexes apart, they have not fought for peaceMinutes and the other's reputation is above minReputation; then a trade agreement when they lack a good the other makes or the other knows more technologies, an alliance when they share an enemy. At most one offer to the same people every offerCooldownMinutes, refusalCooldownMinutes after a refusal. Trade agreements need the barter technology. Barter goods travel in caravans; the AI takes a barter worth acceptWorthPercent of what it gives (100 with currency) and keeps twice what it gives.

roads.comment: Levels of roads. walkPercent: walking cost on them, of the hex's cost (capped at 150 so roads cross rough land). reach: hexes from our nearest settlement. supply: goods carriers bring to a new camp joined to our roads.

seasons.comment: Winter comes every cycleMinutes and lasts winterMinutes (no years: playability first). Work is rounded down to steps of workStepPermille. In winter every worker works at winterWorkPercent; buildings with winterPercent lose that much more (gathering and fields). Peoples are told warnSeconds before.

clothing.comment: Every set of clothing a worker has adds bonusPercent. Outside winter only the first set counts (at most 100+bonus); in winter more sets count, up to winterMaxPercent. Worked out per settlement: sets = clothing in store / people. Sets wear out: wearPerPersonPerMinute.

forage.comment: People of a settlement told to gather pick up food, wood and stone around it. Per gatherer per minute at richness 100: perMinute. A hex's richness: food and wood by biome, stone by relief; deposits and rivers add. A settlement's richness is the mean over the land hexes in its radius (worked out when it is founded or grows).

rivers.comment: Until freeFromEra, rivers can be crossed only next to one's own building that gives a crossing (raft landings).

works.comment: Works drawn on hexes; price and seconds per hex. ditch: farms on watered hexes +farmPercent. palisade: enemies at war standing on it lose woundPercentPerSecond of their people a second. wall: foreign units cannot enter until its strength (hundredths of damage) is broken. aqueduct: a settlement it reaches grows growthBonus% a minute faster and suffers resistEpidemicPercent less from epidemics.

trees.comment: Groves on open land, in clumps: groveChance percent of a biome's land hexes. A grove gives groveWoodPercent of a forest's wood to woodcutters and gatherers.

rations.comment: Every everySeconds a settlement feeds everyone it has: its residents and its units (soldiers, scouts, carriers, settlers on the way), each eating food.foodPerPersonPerMinute for the time since the last ration. Short of food, its units are fed first (fighting ones first), then its workers, then the people without a job: those go hungry first. Hungry people work, gather, fight and walk at hungryPercent. Missed again at the next ration: starvingPercent, and starveLosePercent of the hungry (at least 1) die then and at every further missed ration. One full ration ends it.

startPhase.comment: pickSeconds: time a player has to choose. blockRadius: hexes around a taken start where no other people may start. blockFuzz: the shown circle is centred up to this many hexes from the real start and is this much wider, so it hides the start. scoreRadius, roomRadius: hexes looked at when scoring a start (its own land, the room around).

survey.comment: What is known of the land (Patryk, 2026-11-19). On our own land everything is known. Beyond it, seeing a hex shows only the surface deposits; the rest is found by units that survey (units[].survey): standing still, they look at every hex within radius. rock: prospectors find stone, clay, flint and ores, each ore only from the era in eras (a people recognises an ore once it is in the era of the technology that works it, even before it knows the technology); ores not listed are never found in these eras. soil: surveyors find fertility and the deposits in soil.
